title: Pressure lowers the dust column in tested unconfined gas clouds at the proposed Gaia20cdd radius
abstract: We test pressure expansion in a proposed gas-retention model for Gaia20cdd. An exact Gaussian family of the local isothermal gas equations includes orbital shear and stellar tides. Dust is assumed to move with gas. For a tested cloud at 4 au and 350 K, with mean particle mass 14 hydrogen masses and initial vertical width one stellar radius, the central radial column falls to 0.210 after about 61 days and 0.0643 after about 152 days. A finite uniform stellar disc that initially dims by 3.25 mag dims by at most 0.780 and 0.241 mag at these ages for that column calibration. An initial height of ten stellar radii greatly reduces this loss. Adding gas mass does not slow normalized isothermal expansion. More initial dust column, a larger cloud, cooling, confinement or new supply can change the result. The study adds a pressure test to earlier binding and grain-drift conditions. It does not measure gas, fit a transit or exclude gas retention. Code, model tables, numerical checks, a figure and exact source provenance are included.

display.caption: Column loss and necessary initial optical depth for the tested 4 au Gaussian gas clouds. Model curves assume perfect dust coupling and fixed gas temperature.
